name: Cook 1999: six patterns, counter-clockwise (subjective time)
origin: Cook, Koren & Persinger 1999 (Laurentian University), circumcerebral "Octopus" ring
summary: Cook, Koren & Persinger's 1999 session: six 5-min patterns (three burst-firing, three Thomas) rotated counter-clockwise through eight coils, 2 min apart (40 min). Midway through each you estimate a 10-s interval. The paper reports that 7 people given this direction overestimated 10 s by about 4 s, against about 1 s in 7 people given the clockwise rotation, most with the Thomas pattern at 100 ms plus 20 ms per coil.
notes: Cook 1999 Table 1 lists six configurations: point durations 1, 1, 3, 1, 1, 3 ms; time between repeats 1, 1, 3000, 1, 1, 3000 ms; time on the first solenoid 20, 100, 200, 20, 100, 200 ms; change per solenoid +2, +20, -2, +2, +20, -2 ms (p.2 [62]). The paper reads + as longer: 100, 120, 140 ms ..., and 200 down to 186 ms; its '340 ms at the eighth solenoid' is a misprint for 240 (p.3 [63]). Each configuration ran 5 min with 2 min between files, 40 min in all (p.2-3 [62-63]). The estimate was made midway through each pattern, with the field on (p.2 [62]). This program plays the table in its order, burst-firing (B1 to B3) then Thomas (T1 to T3), one coil at a time, counter-clockwise from Fp1 to Fp2; the site names are this project's reading. The 20 ms row follows the same rule (20 to 34 ms). Booth 2008 reads the same table with + as shorter; persinger-booth-2008-ccw plays that reading, and the papers do not settle which one the lab's software ran. The Thomas pattern plays from the 849-point patent table. The burst-firing point values were never published: the project's rising sweep of 230 points stands in, although the paper says its pattern files held 'between 300 and 10,000 points' (p.3 [63]). The paper gives 5 to 10 uT adjacent to the scalp (p.2 [62]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 5 uT the scalp gets about 120 uT, 12 to 24 times the paper's value; about 0.3 uT matches it. 14 people, 7 per direction, told the study was about relaxation; no sham group; single lab, never independently replicated. Time estimates are easily swayed by expectation. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Seated or reclined, eyes closed, in a quiet, dim room. Midway through each 5-min pattern (2.5 min in, with the field on), mark the start and end of what feels like 10 s for a helper with a stopwatch (or on a stopwatch you cannot see) and write down the result.
schedule: One session in the original, which compared two groups. For a self-test, run this and the clockwise version on different days in blinded, random order and compare the 10-s estimates.
source: Cook, Koren & Persinger 1999, Subjective time estimation by humans is increased by counterclockwise but not clockwise circumcerebral rotations of phase-shifting magnetic pulses in the horizontal plane, Neurosci Lett 268:61-64 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10400078/ ; Persinger, Roll, Tiller, Koren & Cook 2002, Percept Mot Skills 94:927-949 (Table 1, six configurations) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12081299/ ; Persinger & Lavallee 2010, J Conscious Explor Res 1(7):785-807 (20+2 notation; coil 1 left frontal, coil 8 right prefrontal) https://jcer.com/index.php/jcj/article/view/99 ; Saroka 2016, PhD dissertation, Laurentian University (Cook 1999 rotated the Thomas pulse with "the Octopus") https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/be015982-0b0f-4c27-a031-797637c364e1/content ; Thomas, Prato, Kavaliers & Persinger, US 6,234,953 B1, Table 1 (Thomas pulse point values) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6234953B1/en ; Buckner et al. 2015, PLoS ONE 10(4) (Thomas file: 849 points at 3 ms, 2.55 s per cycle) https://europepmc.org/article/MED/25875081 ; Booth, Koren & Persinger 2008, Electromagn Biol Med 27:426-436 (clockwise vs counter-clockwise) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19037792/ ; Koren & Persinger, US 6,312,376 B1 (sequence interval and sequence acceleration) https://patents.google.com/patent/US6312376B1/en ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1-6 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
